maria: quick question — running into weird dims when streaming embeddings with the python SDK. batcher returns 1536 for some items and 1024 for others, causing downstream faiss insert to crash. anyone seen this?

aj: is this with the rerank pipeline or a raw embed call?

maria: raw embed streaming + retries enabled. sometimes retry returns a full vector, sometimes a truncated one (looks like partial chunk). here's simplified code: 
```python
resp = client.embeddings.stream(model="embed-v1", inputs=batch)
for r in resp:
    # r.embedding length varies...
    print(len(r.embedding))
```

liam: can you paste an example response or error snippet? also are you using token rotation/auth middleware? we once saw a bug where a 401 retry returned a cached partial body.

maria: error: "IndexError: dim mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024". no obvious 401 in logs around the call, but i do see a fallback log: "routed to embed-lite due to capacity" right before some of the responses.

aj: two possible causes: (1) model routing fallback returning a different dimensionality, (2) stream chunks being emitted per-chunk and not assembled before using. some SDK stream helpers yield partial chunk payloads; you must assemble until final. e.g.
```python
embeds = []
for chunk in client.embeddings.stream(...):
    if chunk.type == 'partial':
        buffer.extend(chunk.data)
    elif chunk.type == 'final':
        embeds.append(assemble(buffer))
        buffer.clear()
```

sophia: also check the model metadata endpoint — `/models/embed-v1` returns `vector_size`. run a quick curl to confirm what the server believes the model size is when you hit it (helps catch routing issues):
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/models/embed-v1 | jq .vector_size
```

dev-bot: deploy succeeded: cd/embeds-service @maria :rocket:

maria: aha — looks like the routing fallback is the culprit. during spikes we fall back to `embed-lite` (1024) which currently returns 200 + embeddings but different dims. client assumes consistent dim and blows up.

ryan: ugh. we shouldn't silently accept incompatible model variants. two quick mitigations: server-side validation that enforces consistent `vector_size` for a model alias, and client-side assert: `if len(vec) != expected_dim: raise ValueError(...)` and log the model id.

aj: agreed. also for the batching/pagination helper — if you're concatenating pages make sure you re-pad/truncate per-item instead of at the end; page boundaries + streaming can produce partial vectors if you `extend` raw bytes instead of assembling records.

sophia: i'll open a PR to the python client to: add dimensionality check on response, add opt-in `allow_fallback_models` flag (default false), and add a small helper to assemble streaming chunks safely. i'll ping eng-ml for review.

maria: thanks! i'll attach a minimal reproducer and the failing vectors to the issue so tests can cover it.

liam: re: auth middleware race — i flagged a token-refresh race in #3251. i pushed a small fix to ensure in-flight retries use the refreshed token. if you still see 401+partial responses after the client patch, tag me and i'll re-open.

aj: quick review ping when PR is up — will look at the assemble helper and tests. :thumbsup:

sophia: opened draft PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432 (adding checks + flag + tests). cc @aj @liam @maria

maria: perfect, i'll drop the reproducer into the PR and run it against canary. thanks y'all. :pray:
